deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is German prose, apparently lecture or reading notes on ancient Persian history, continuing from folio 38 (Cyrus, Cambyses, Smerdis). The content runs as follows.

(1) Cambyses' expeditions against the oracle of Jupiter Ammon and against Ethiopia were dispatched but failed.

(2) Back in Egypt, Cambyses learns of a conspiracy in inner Asia: a man calling himself Smerdis now sits on the throne.

(3) Mounting his horse on hearing the news, Cambyses accidentally wounds himself fatally with his own sword. He reigned 529-522 BC.

(4) Pseudo-Smerdis holds the throne only 8 months. He remits tribute to the subject peoples to win their favour. This embitters the Persians, and seven Persian nobles form a conspiracy. They force their way into the palace and murder Pseudo-Smerdis.

(5) The choice of king is left to an oracle; a parenthesis notes that the chief god was the Sun. The lot falls on Darius I, who takes the throne in 522 and reigns 522-486, i.e. 36 years.

(6) Early in his reign Babylon revolts. Darius recovers it only by a ruse, with the help of Zopyrus.

(7) He then turns to Europe. His first great campaign is against the Scythians, with an army of 100000 men. The Scythians withdraw; this continues on the next page.

There are no formulas, computations or derivations to reconstruct. The page sits in a Gauss Nachlass bundle labelled 'HB.Lagrange1816', but its content is history notes; the authorship and the reason it is in this bundle cannot be determined from the page alone.
errors: Chronology: Cambyses is usually dated 530-522 BC; the notes give 529 for Cyrus' death and Cambyses' accession, an older traditional dating rather than a slip.
In Herodotus (III.84-87) Darius is chosen by the neighing of his horse at sunrise, not by an oracle or lot. The note's 'Orakel'/'Loos' with the Sun as chief god is a loose paraphrase of this story.
Herodotus (IV.87) gives Darius' Scythian army as 700,000 men. The notes have 100000, possibly a lecturer's or copyist's figure.

results.what: Historical narrative of Cambyses, Pseudo-Smerdis and Darius I (non-mathematical)
results.modern_name: Achaemenid history after Herodotus Book III-IV

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine ancient-history notes with no mathematical content. Nothing here bears on Gauss's mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Darius I's reign 522-486 BC has the stated length of 36 years
The stated reign of Cambyses, 529-522 BC, lasts 7 years

So the intended reading is 'Die Verschwörenen drangen in den Pallast', and the separate 'ein' is doubtful.
